what: The score combines the fixed-position insertion-distance increase with two one-step signals: a reward for the largest feasible Clarke–Wright-style depot saving to another unassigned customer, and a small penalty for capacity left unused after the best one-customer continuation. It scans only the current route and unassigned list, so each call costs O(len(route) + len(unassigned)) time and O(1) extra space.
why: Immediate insertion cost promotes geometric coherence, while the saving term favors candidates that can later share a route with a nearby feasible customer—an adjacency that intra-route 2-opt may exploit. The modest packing term discourages choices likely to close a route with avoidable residual capacity, which is relevant with heterogeneous demands. The coefficients keep immediate geometry dominant. This remains a local, one-step construction heuristic: it does not predict later route openings, account for interactions among several future customers, or guarantee improvement on held-out instances.
